title: Upper Airway Morphology and Physiology During Graded Positive Pressure and Nasal High Flow: An MRI Study
official: Effects of Graded Positive Airway Pressure and Nasal High Flow Interfaces on Upper Airway Morphology and Breathing Physiology in Healthy Volunteers and COPD Patients: A Controlled MRI Study
summary: This study investigates the effects of graded nasal high flow (NHF) and continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) on upper airway morphology and respiratory physiology in healthy volunteers and patients with COPD. Participants undergo baseline MRI and physiological assessment followed by NHF at 30 and 60 L/min and CPAP at 4 and 12 cmH₂O. The primary aim is to determine whether graded NHF and CPAP induce dose-dependent changes in upper airway morphology, including upper airway volume and cross-sectional area, during MRI scans.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Written informed consent
* Age ≥18 years
* BMI ≤30 kg/m²

Exclusion Criteria:

* Inability or refusal to provide informed consent
* Contraindications to MRI (e.g., claustrophobia or ferromagnetic implants)
* Contraindications to mask-based positive airway pressure or nasal high flow
* Pregnancy
* Physical or mental conditions limiting study participation or compliance, as judged by the investigator
* Alcohol, drug, medication, or other substance abuse
* Any other objective reason preventing study participation, as determined by the investigator
